capabilities.name: ontology
capabilities.description: Emit the complete ATP ontology for agent discovery.

capabilities.name: explain
capabilities.description: Say what a command will do before it runs. The tool's own dry-run affordance.

capabilities.name: validate
capabilities.description: Check a pattern, expression or pipeline without executing it.

capabilities.name: scope
capabilities.description: List the files the scope configuration selects.

capabilities.name: query
capabilities.description: Execute an AQL query. Read or replace depending on the query.

capabilities.name: context
capabilities.description: Show surrounding lines for each match.

capabilities.name: compliance
capabilities.description: NIST FIPS and CMMC 2.0 reporting, and SHA-256 integrity hashes.

capabilities.name: transform
capabilities.description: Pattern-based substitution across files, sed-like. Rewrites content.

capabilities.name: pipeline
capabilities.description: Run a multi-stage pipeline, which may include transforms.

capabilities.name: watch
capabilities.description: Re-run a query whenever files change. Runs until stopped.

capabilities.name: mcp
capabilities.description: Serve ATP tools over JSON-RPC for agents. Runs until stopped.

note: Neither field is derived. This tool enumerates its commands but declares no effect, safety or authority data, so requires_grant and budgeted are judgements made from command semantics and are labelled as such rather than presented as the tool's own position. Replace this file with a derived one if the tool ever declares effects, the way abt, Rodeo, Botnet, MAGE and HyperMachine do. The rule applied: a grant is required to rewrite files, change configuration, or run until stopped. transform and pipeline rewrite content; watch, repl and mcp hold the process open; config changes defaults. search, analyze, context, scope and compliance only read, but each scans a caller-specified file set, so they are budgeted while ungranted. query is granted because AQL expresses both find and replace in one syntax, so the command name alone cannot tell a caller which they are getting -- the conservative reading is the correct one for a grant. ATP ships explain for exactly this ambiguity, and a caller unsure what a query will do should run it first.
